q: 1. To obtain cement dry powder, lime stones and shales or their slurry, is burnt in a rotary kiln at a temperature between
explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix is burnt at 1400°C–1500°C, the clinkering temperature, at which the raw materials fuse to form cement clinker.

q: 2. The maximum quantity of ingredients present in cement production is
explain: Lime (CaO) forms the largest proportion (about 60-65%) of the chemical composition of cement, hence it is present in maximum quantity.

q: 3. The mixture of different ingredients of cement is burnt at
explain: In the rotary kiln, the raw mix of calcareous and argillaceous materials is burnt at about 1400-1500°C to form clinker, and the closest listed value is 1400°C.

q: 4. Addition of pozzolana to ordinary portland cement, causes
options: reduction in chemical action with sulphates
explain: Addition of pozzolana affects cement in all these ways: it lowers early strength, reduces sulphate attack, increases shrinkage slightly, and reduces bleeding, hence all statements are correct.

q: 5. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very fast with water, is chiefly responsible for the initial set, and releases a large amount of heat of hydration.

q: 6. Pozzolana cement is used with confidence for
explain: Due to its low heat of hydration and resistance to chemical attack, pozzolana cement is confidently used in dams, massive foundations, abutments, and RCC structures.

q: 7. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1: 3 cement mortar cube) after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS specifications, a 1:3 cement-sand mortar cube of ordinary Portland cement must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 17.5 N/mm² after 7 days.

q: 8. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of .... by weight of cement
explain: For the initial and final setting time tests, water is added at the rate of 0.85 times the water needed for standard consistency (P), i.e., 0.85P, as per IS code.

q: 9. The aggregates of ......shape have minimum voids.
explain: Rounded aggregates pack more closely together, minimizing the void content compared to angular, irregular, or flaky shapes.

q: 10. The material having particle size varying from 0.002 to 0.06 mm is termed as
explain: Particles with size between roughly 0.002 mm and 0.06 (0.075) mm fall in the silt size classification, between clay and sand.

q: 11. The aggregate is said to be elongated when
options: its least dimension is three fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal 1.8 times of its mean dimension
explain: As defined in this text, an aggregate particle is classified as elongated when its length exceeds 1.8 times its mean sieve dimension.

q: 12. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: continuous grading is not necessary for obtaining a minimum of air voids
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
the omission of a certain size of aggregate is shown by straight horizontal line on the grading curve
explain: The grading curve shows a horizontal straight-line segment when a particular size fraction is missing (gap grading), and continuous grading isn't essential for minimum voids; hence all of the above are correct.

q: 13. If the aggregates completely pass through a sieve of size 75mm and are retained on a sieve of size 60mm, the particular aggregate will be flaky if its minimum dimension is less than
explain: Mean size = (75+60)/2 = 67.5mm; flaky if least dimension < 3/5 × mean size = 0.6 × 67.5 ≈ 40.5mm.

q: 14. In Q. No. 70 the aggregates will be known as elongated aggregate if its length is not less than
explain: Elongated if length ≥ 1.8 × mean size = 1.8 × 67.5 = 121.5mm (using the thrice-mean-size type criterion referenced in these questions).

q: 15. Finer grinding of cement
options: affects only the early development of strength
explain: Finer grinding increases the surface area available for hydration, which speeds up early reaction and improves early strength development, without significantly changing the ultimate (long-term) strength.

q: 16. The most useless aggregate is, whose surface texture is
explain: A glossy surface texture prevents good bonding between the aggregate and the cement paste, making it the least useful/desirable aggregate surface type.

q: 17. The aggregate impact value of the aggregate used in
options: road pavement concrete is less than 30
explain: As per IS specifications, the aggregate impact value limits given for building concrete (<45), road pavement (<30), and runway concrete (<30) are all correct.

q: 18. The creep strains are
options: caused due to dead loads only
caused due to live loads only
explain: Creep is the time-dependent deformation of concrete under sustained/continued stress, which can result from both dead and live loads acting over time.

q: 19. The void ratio of
options: single size coarse aggregate is roughly 0.45
explain: The void ratios given for single size coarse aggregate, graded coarse aggregate, and fine aggregate are all approximately correct as standard values.

q: 20. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: the bulk density of fine aggregate is usually about 10 percent more than that of coarse aggregate of similar composition
the specific gravity of aggregate is important for the determination of the moisture content
the absorption and porosity of an aggregate, influence the property of the concrete
a highly absorptive aggregate reduces the workability of concrete considerably
explain: All statements about bulk density comparison, specific gravity's role, and absorption/porosity effects on concrete workability are correct.

q: 21. The strength and durability of concrete depends
explain: Strength and durability of concrete are collectively influenced by aggregate size, grading, and moisture content, among other factors — hence all of these apply.

q: 22. A ordinary Portland cement when tested for its fineness, should not leave any residue on I.S. sieve No. 9, more than
explain: As per IS specifications, ordinary Portland cement's residue retained on the 90-micron (IS sieve No. 9) sieve should not exceed 10% by weight.

q: 23. In lime concrete, lime is used as
explain: In lime concrete, lime acts as the cementitious/binding material that holds the aggregate particles together, analogous to the role cement plays in cement concrete.

q: 24. Concrete mainly consists of
explain: Concrete is a composite material made primarily of cement (binder), aggregates (fine and coarse), and water, combined and allowed to harden through hydration.

q: 25. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following. For performing compressive strength test of cement
options: Cement and standard sand mortar are used in the ratio of 1:3
Water is added at the rate of P/4 + 3.0 percentage of water, where P is the percentage of water for standard consistency
A cube mould of 10cm x 10cm x 10cm is used
The prepared moulds are kept in an atmosphere of 50% relative humidity
explain: This is incorrect: the standard cube mould used for the cement compressive strength (mortar cube) test is 7.06 cm (70.6 mm) size, not 10 cm x 10 cm x 10 cm.

q: 26. If fineness modulus of sand is 2.5, it is graded as
explain: As per the fineness modulus classification used in this text, a value of 2.5 places the sand in the 'fine sand' category.

q: 27. Adding a thin layer of cement mortar to the surface of concrete is known as
explain: Rendering (rendeting) refers to applying a thin coat/layer of cement mortar over a concrete or masonry surface, typically for finishing or protective purposes.

q: 28. Which of the following ingredient of cement when added in excess quantity, causes the cement to set slowly?
explain: Excess silica in cement slows down the setting process, as silicates react and hydrate more slowly compared to aluminates.

q: 29. The center needle of attachment of the vicat plunger projects the circular cutting edge by
explain: In the Vicat apparatus attachment used for final setting time, the center needle projects beyond the circular cutting edge by 0.5 mm.

q: 30. Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured from
explain: As per the answer key, ordinary Portland cement's raw materials given here are gypsum and lime, gypsum being added to control setting time along with the limestone-derived lime compounds.

q: 31. For the construction of cement concrete floor, the maximum permissible size of aggregate is
explain: For thin concrete floor toppings/finishes, the maximum permissible coarse aggregate size is limited to about 10 mm to allow a smooth, thin surface layer.

q: 32. Cement used for normal concrete construction, is obtained by burning a mixture of
explain: Ordinary Portland cement is manufactured by burning a mixture containing siliceous, argillaceous, and calcareous raw materials together to form clinker.

q: 33. Blast furnace slag cement
explain: Blast furnace slag cement develops both a lower heat of hydration and comparatively lower early strength than OPC, so both a and b are correct.

q: 34. If the depth of moist sand in a cylinder is 15 cm and the depth of the sand with fully inundated with water is 12 cm, the bulking of the moist sand, is
explain: Bulking % = [(h1 - h2)/h2] x 100 = [(15-12)/12] x 100 = 25%, where h1 is the moist sand depth and h2 is the fully inundated (saturated) depth.

q: 35. According to Indian standards, the pozzolana content in Portland pozzolana cement is
explain: As per IS 1489, the pozzolana content permitted in Portland Pozzolana Cement (PPC) ranges from 10% to 25% by mass.

q: 36. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinker is about
explain: As given in this text, about 30% pozzolanic material is blended with OPC clinker in the manufacture of pozzolana cement.

q: 37. The fineness of cement is measured in terms of
options: percentage of weight retained on is sieve no. 9
surface area in cm2 per gram of the cement
explain: Cement fineness can be expressed either as the percentage retained on the standard 90-micron sieve or as specific surface area (Blaine's method) — either of these two measures is used.

q: 38. Durability of cement concrete generally improves by
explain: Increasing the cement content generally produces denser, less permeable concrete, which improves its overall durability.

q: 39. In vicats apparatus, the diameter of vicat plunger is
explain: The standard Vicat plunger used for the consistency test has a diameter of 10 mm.

q: 40. If the effective plan area of a ware house is 54 m2 and the maximum height of pile permitted is 2.7 m, then the number of cement bags to be stored is
explain: Using the standard storage capacity formula for a floor area of 54 m² and pile height of 2.7 m, the number of bags works out to approximately 2700.

q: 41. Under normal conditions using an ordinary cement, the period of removal of the form work is
options: 14 days for bottom of slabs of spans 4.6 m and more
21 days for bottom of beams over 6m spans
2 days for vertical sides of columns
explain: These are all standard specified formwork removal periods (as per IS code guidance) for different structural elements under normal conditions using ordinary cement, so all of the above is correct.

q: 42. As compared to ordinary Portland cement, use of pozzolanic cement
explain: Pozzolanic cement, due to its finer particles and pozzolanic reaction characteristics, tends to increase the drying shrinkage of concrete as compared to OPC.

q: 43. Vicat apparatus is used for
explain: The primary and original use of the Vicat apparatus (with the standard plunger) is to determine the standard consistency of cement paste.

q: 44. If sea water is used for preparing concrete mix, it
explain: Sea water contains salts that reduce concrete strength, promote corrosion of embedded steel reinforcement, and cause efflorescence — all of these harmful effects occur.

q: 45. Expansive cement expands mostly during its :
explain: Expansive cement is engineered so that most of its expansion occurs during the final hardening period, after initial set, to compensate for later drying shrinkage.

q: 46. For the construction of cement concrete floor the maximum permissible sizes of aggregate is :
explain: For thin concrete floor toppings/finishes, the maximum permissible aggregate size is limited to 10 mm to allow a smooth, well-finished surface.

q: 47. The cement-sad ratio used in the compressive strength test of cement as per the Indian Standard Specification is :
explain: As per Indian Standard Specification, the compressive strength test of cement is performed using a standard mortar of cement-sand ratio 1:3.
